title: Should You Buy AMD Stock Before the Huge Investor Update?
creator: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA
summary: Parkevtate Vosianc answers whether AMD's 16% one-month dip (from over $650) is a buying opportunity before its 3 Nov earnings: no, with medium conviction — wait until after the print. The fundamentals are strong: data-centre revenue more than doubled year over year, total revenue rose 50%, operating income swung to $2B from -$134M (margin 17% versus -2%), and he expects Q3 revenue above the roughly $13B guide, closer to $14-15B, on AI demand that keeps beating expectations every quarter since ChatGPT's launch. But valuation blocks the buy: AMD trades at 33.6x forward earnings, more than twice Nvidia's multiple, and his model puts fair value at $394 versus a $531 market price — the same models that flagged AMD as overvalued about a month ago, since when it has fallen 16%. He also warns the 'alternative to Nvidia' thesis is fading as Amazon and Alphabet push their own chips. Other tickers discussed: Nvidia (65%+ operating margin, the comparison), Meta (Meta Muse personal agent, over 10M downloads, as a consumer-AI catalyst). Calls made: AMD — HOLD reiterated (was HOLD 9 Oct, no flip); he had ranked AMD a buy for years before downgrading it about a month ago.

calls.video_title: Should You Buy AMD Stock Before the Huge Investor Update?
calls.thesis: HOLD reiterated (was HOLD 2026-10-09; no flip) — not a buying opportunity on the dip before the 3 Nov earnings; if interested, wait until after the print. Data-centre revenue more than doubled, but at 33.6x forward earnings (2x Nvidia) he still calls it stretched.
calls.bull_case: Data-centre-led revenue +50%, operating margin -2% to 17%, and he expects Q3 revenue above the ~$13B guide, nearer $14-15B.
calls.bear_case: Fair value $394 vs $531 market, proprietary chips from Amazon/Alphabet eroding the 'Nvidia alternative' case, and Nvidia's 65%+ operating margin vs AMD's 17%.
